**Commentary of Ibn al-Jawzi (Zad al-Masir) on Surah 96, verses 6–19:**

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, no!﴾ meaning: truly. Muqatil said: ﴿No!﴾ (means) he does not know that Allah taught him. Then He resumed and said, Exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, man transgresses﴾, meaning Abu Jahl. Whenever he acquired wealth, he became arrogant and insolent in his clothing, his mounts, and his food. ﴿When he sees himself as self-sufficient﴾. Ibn Qutayba said: meaning, when he sees himself as self-sufficient. And "al-Ruj'a" means the return.

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Have you seen the one who forbids﴾. The meaning of "ara'ayt" (have you seen): it is an expression of wonder directed at the addressee. He repeated it for emphasis and to express wonder. The one intended by "the forbidder" here is Abu Jahl. Abu Hurayra said: (p-177) Abu Jahl said: "Does Muhammad rub his face in the dust among you?" They said: "Yes." He said: "By the One by whom I swear, if I see him, I will certainly step on his neck." It was said to him: "There he is, praying." So he set off to step on his neck, but they were suddenly startled to see him backing away on his heels and shielding himself with his hands. They came to him and said: "What is wrong with you, Abu al-Hakam?" He said: "Between me and him is a trench of fire, a terror, and wings." The Prophet of Allah (ﷺ) said: "By the One in whose hand is my soul, if he had come near me, the angels would have snatched him, limb by limb." Then Allah revealed: ﴿Have you seen the one who forbids﴾ to the end of the surah. Ibn Abbas said: "The Prophet (ﷺ) was praying, when Abu Jahl came and said: 'Did I not forbid you from this?!' The Prophet (ﷺ) turned toward him and rebuked him. Abu Jahl said: 'By Allah, you know that no one in this valley has more followers than I do.' So Allah revealed: ﴿Then let him call his associates﴾ ﴿We will call the guards of Hell﴾." Ibn Abbas said: "By Allah, if he had called his associates, the angels of punishment of Allah would have seized him."

The exegetes said: the "servant" intended here is Muhammad (ﷺ). It was also said that the prayer was the Dhuhr prayer.

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Have you seen if he is upon guidance﴾, meaning the one who is forbidden, who is the Prophet (ﷺ).

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Have you seen if he denies and turns away﴾, meaning the forbidder, who is Abu Jahl. Al-Farra' said: the meaning is: Have you seen the one who forbids a servant when he prays, while he himself is a liar who turns away from the remembrance? So what could be more astonishing than this?! Ibn al-Anbari said: its implied meaning is: "Have you seen him being right?"

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Does he not know that Allah sees﴾, meaning Abu Jahl, ﴿that (act)﴾ and will recompense him for it. ﴿No!﴾ meaning: he does not know that. ﴿If he does not desist﴾ from denying Muhammad, reviling him, and harming him, ﴿We will surely seize him by the forelock﴾. "Al-saf'" means seizing, and "al-nasiyah" is the front of the head. Abu Ubayda said: it is said, "I seized (safa'tu) with his hand," (p-179) meaning I took hold of it with it. Al-Zajjaj said: it is said, "I seized the thing" when you grasp it and pull it with a strong pull. The meaning is: We will drag his forelock into the Fire.

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿forelock﴾. Abu Ubayda said: it is a substitute (badal), which is why it is in the genitive case. Al-Zajjaj said: the meaning is: "by a forelock whose owner is a liar, a sinner," just as it is said: "his day is fasting and his night is standing," meaning he fasts during his day and stands in prayer during his night. ﴿Then let him call his associates﴾, meaning the people of his assembly, who are his companions, so let him seek their help. ﴿We will call the guards of Hell﴾. Ata said: they are the harsh, severe angels. Muqatil said: they are the keepers of Hell. Qatada said: in the language of the Arabs, "al-zabaniyah" are the police. Al-Farra' said: al-Kisa'i used to say: "I have not heard a singular form for al-zabaniyah." Then he said later: "The singular of al-zabaniyah is zibniy, but I do not know whether this is by analogy from it or by hearing." Ibn Qutayba said: it is derived from al-zabn, which is pushing, as though they push the people of the Fire into it. Ibn Duraid said: al-zabn is pushing. It is said: "a she-camel is zabun if she pushes away her milker and kicks him with her leg." And "tazabana al-qawm" means they repelled one another. The derivation of "al-zabaniyah" is from al-zabn. And Allah knows best.

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿No!﴾ meaning: the matter is not as Abu Jahl is (upon). ﴿Do not obey him﴾ in abandoning the prayer. ﴿Prostrate﴾, meaning: pray to Allah. ﴿And draw near﴾ to Him through obedience. This is the view of the majority: that His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿and draw near﴾, is addressed to the Prophet (ﷺ). It has also been said that it is addressed to Abu Jahl. Then there are two views on this.

(p-180) One of them: the meaning is: "Prostrate, you O Muhammad, and draw near, you O Abu Jahl, to the Fire." This was said by Zayd ibn Aslam.

The second: "And draw near, O Abu Jahl," as a threat to him. This was narrated by Abu Sulayman al-Dimashqi from some of the early scholars. This is explained by the hadith of Abu Hurayra that we mentioned earlier. Abu Hurayra narrated from the Prophet (ﷺ) that he said: "The closest a servant is to his Lord is when he is prostrating, so increase your supplication."
